title: Bug Catcher Arcade
intro: Catch errors before they crash your program, and import powerful modules! First-try wins earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: Which pair safely handles code that might cause an error?
rounds.explain: try runs the risky code; except catches the error so your program doesn't crash.
Dividing by zero causes an error, so Python jumps to except and prints the safe message.
math.sqrt finds the square root. The square root of 16 is 4.0.

rounds.prompt: We want to use random but forgot something. Pick the fix.
options: Add import random at the top
rounds.explain: Before using a toolkit like random, you must import it first.

rounds.prompt: Why do we use except in a try block?
options: To run a backup plan when something goes wrong
To make the code run faster
rounds.explain: except is your safety net, it catches problems and lets the program keep going.

rounds.prompt: Build a try/except that warns when dividing by zero.
rounds.explain: Risky code goes under try, and the rescue message goes under except.
